claims: As of March and April 2026, COVID-19 continues to circulate.
As of March and April 2026, new highly mutated Omicron subvariants serve as a major driver of COVID-19 cases in the U.S. and globally.
BA.3.2 "Cicada" variant is a notable highly mutated Omicron subvariant.
COVID-19 symptoms in 2026 are very similar to symptoms of other circulating respiratory infections such as the flu, RSV, and the common cold.
2026 COVID-19 variants generally produce mild to moderate symptoms.
Symptoms of 2026 COVID-19 variants often start in the upper respiratory tract.
Severe or "Razorblade" sore throat is a common symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Severe or "Razorblade" sore throat is distinct, sharp, or intensely painful.
Persistent cough is a common symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Persistent cough from 2026 COVID-19 is usually a dry hacking cough.
Runny or stuffy nose is a common symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Runny or stuffy nose from 2026 COVID-19 involves significant nasal congestion.
Fatigue and muscle aches are common symptoms of 2026 COVID-19.
Fatigue and muscle aches from 2026 COVID-19 involve lingering tiredness and body aches.
Headache is a frequently reported symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Fever or chills are common symptoms of 2026 COVID-19.
Fever or chills from 2026 COVID-19 are sometimes milder than in earlier years.
Sneezing is a common symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Sneezing from 2026 COVID-19 often makes it hard to distinguish from a cold.
BA.3.2 "Cicada" variant is characterized by its ability to evade immune protection due to high mutations in the spike protein.
BA.3.2 "Cicada" variant is highly contagious.
"Stratus" variant is a sub-variant spreading in 2026.
"Stratus" variant often causes "scratchy" or raspy voices.
"Stratus" variant causes symptoms similar to "razor throat".
Loss of taste or smell is a possible symptom of 2026 COVID-19.
Loss of taste or smell is reported less frequently in 2026 than in early pandemic years.
Loss of taste or smell remains a strong indicator of 2026 COVID-19 if present.
As of March 2026, research shows that Long COVID symptoms can persist for over 2.5 years.
Common long-term effects of Long COVID include severe dyspnea.
Common long-term effects of Long COVID include cognitive dysfunction ("brain fog").
Common long-term effects of Long COVID include profound fatigue.
